title: The Quran: Surah 105, al-Fil (The Elephant)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 105. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to verse 3, what did He send against them?
questions.why: O versículo 3 diz: 'He sent against them swarms of birds.'

questions.q: Verse 2 says 'make their plan go wrong'. What does this tell you about the People of the Elephant?
options: They had a plan, and it did not succeed
questions.why: O texto diz que o plano deles correu mal.

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up the passage?
options: Their plan failed, and birds and rocks left them like chewed-up leaves
questions.why: Os versículos 2 a 5 descrevem o que lhes aconteceu.

B2.discussion: The passage begins with two questions. Why might a story start with questions instead of facts?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Tell the events of the passage in the order they appear.

questions.q: How does verse 5 describe the People of the Elephant?
questions.why: O versículo 5 diz: 'Leaving them like chewed-up leaves.'

questions.q: 'Rocks of baked clay' is closest to:
Which order of events does the passage give?
options: Swarms of birds are sent, rocks are thrown, they are left like chewed-up leaves
They are left like chewed-up leaves, then birds are sent
Rocks are thrown, then the plan is made
The plan is made, then they win
questions.why: O versículo 3 manda os pássaros, o 4 atira pedras e o 5 descreve o resultado.

questions.q: Verses 1 and 2 are questions. What are verses 3 to 5?
What does the comparison in verse 5 do?
options: It shows the outcome by a vivid image of something chewed and left over
questions.why: 'Like chewed-up leaves' dá uma imagem concreta do resultado.

C1.discussion: The passage opens with two questions and answers them with three short descriptions. How does this question and answer order shape the way the reader takes in the events?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how verses 3 to 5 develop the events in order.

questions.q: In verse 4, the word 'Throwing' continues the action of:
options: the swarms of birds in verse 3
questions.why: O versículo 3 fala de 'swarms of birds' e o versículo 4 continua com 'Throwing'.

questions.q: Verses 4 and 5 begin with 'Throwing' and 'Leaving'. What kind of words are they?
options: Verbs ending in -ing that continue the action of verse 3
questions.why: 'Throwing' e 'Leaving' continuam a acção do versículo 3.

questions.q: The opening questions ('Have you not considered...', 'Did He not make...') invite which kind of answer?
options: A yes: they invite the reader to agree
questions.why: Perguntas formuladas com 'not' convidam o leitor a concordar.

questions.q: Which description of the structure is most accurate?
options: Two questions, then an action (verse 3) continued by two -ing phrases (verses 4 and 5)
questions.why: O versículo 3 descreve a acção e os versículos 4 e 5 continuam-na com 'Throwing' e 'Leaving'.

questions.q: Which statement is best supported by the passage as a whole?
options: It moves from questions to a concrete sequence of events that ends in a vivid image
questions.why: Os versículos 1 e 2 são perguntas e os versículos 3 a 5 descrevem os acontecimentos.

C2.discussion: Verses 4 and 5 continue the action of verse 3 with -ing phrases. What does this continuous flow do to the pace of the passage?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how questions, sequence and imagery work together in the five verses, referring to specific words.
